unit.title: Helpers that act: steps, tools and asking first

lesson.title: The helper’s toolbox
lesson.subtitle: Picking the right tool, saying “I can’t”, and asking

video.title: The helper’s toolbox
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya (main character)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice, talking to the student (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: A list: Book a ticket; “I can’t”; No such tool.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: I asked my helper to book a bus ticket to the city. It said: sorry, I can’t do that! Was it being lazy? No: it just didn’t have that tool.

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: a helper and its toolbox.

scenes.visual: A list: Weather; Calculator; Timetable; Route.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A helper has a toolbox. Darsi Tiny has ten tools: the weather, a calculator, the timetable, reminders, a route finder, and more. It can only do the jobs its tools can do.

scenes.visual: A list: How far to Dala? The route tool; 17 × 23? The calculator.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: It picks the tool that fits
scenes.narration: For each question, it picks the tool that fits. How far is it to Dala? The route tool. What is seventeen times twenty-three? The calculator.

scenes.visual: A list: No tool fits the job; “I can’t do that”; Honest is good.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: When no tool fits the job, a good helper says so. Book a ticket? I can’t: none of my tools can do that. That’s honest, and that’s good!

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: And when something is missing, it asks you. What’s the weather tomorrow? Which village? Once you say Dala, it uses the weather tool.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! You ask: will it rain in Sabo tomorrow? Which tool should the helper pick?

scenes.visual: A list: Tool: weather; Place: Sabo; Day: tomorrow; The right details, like a form.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The weather tool, with the place, Sabo, and the day, tomorrow. A tool needs the right details, like a form you fill in.

scenes.visual: A list: You asked: class 9Z; It wrote: class 9C!; Check what it filled in.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Helpers can still guess wrong. I asked about class 9Z, which doesn’t exist. Darsi Tiny wrote 9C, a different class! So check what it filled in.

scenes.visual: A list: Ask for the weather; Switch the tool off; What does it say?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, you can switch tools off. Ask for the weather, then switch the weather tool off and ask again. What does the helper say now?

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. You ask the helper to buy you new shoes, but it has no shopping tool. What should a good helper say?

scenes.visual: Summary points: It picks the tool that fits; No tool? “I can’t”; Something missing? It asks.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: It picks the tool that fits · No tool? “I can’t” · Something missing? It asks
scenes.narration: Sorry, I can’t: that’s the honest answer. Remember: a helper picks the tool that fits. With no tool, it says I can’t. And when something is missing, it asks.

scenes.visual: A list: A toolbox of cards; One tool on each card; Your friend asks; Pick, ask, or say “I can’t”.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it yourself: make a toolbox of cards with a friend. Write one tool on each card: weather, calculator, timetable. Your friend asks things, and you pick a card, ask what’s missing, or say I can’t!

checkpoints.prompt: You ask: will it rain in Sabo tomorrow? Which tool should the helper pick?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — rain is weather, so it picks the weather tool, with the place Sabo and the day tomorrow.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — rain is about the weather, so the weather tool fits.

checkpoints.prompt: You ask the helper to buy you new shoes, but it has no shopping tool. What should a good helper say?

options.text: “Done! Your shoes are on the way.”

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — with no tool for the job, the honest answer is “I can’t”. Pretending would be worse.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — it has no shopping tool, so it can’t buy anything. The honest answer is “I can’t”.
